# ADR 0010: Components ship a prebuilt stylesheet

**Status:** accepted on 2026-11-06.

**Context.** `@croffcss/ui` offers components on top of CROFF. A project's scanner always ignores `node_modules`, so it can't see the classes inside an installed package, and asking people to change that would slow every scan.

**Decision.** The package ships `styles.css`, generated by `croff build` from the classes in `src/recipes.ts`. Components are functions that return class names, so they work in any framework, and the React components are a thin layer over them. Colors, fonts and sizes are custom properties, so restyling doesn't need a rebuild. Every token is emitted, including those no component uses, so that any of them can be overridden.

**Consequences.**

- Using the components doesn't require CROFF's build tools. A project can use the stylesheet alone.
- A project using both ships some rules twice, when its own classes match a component's. They're identical, so the result is the same.
- The whole stylesheet is loaded, even for one component. Only the rules a project uses would be smaller, but that would need the scanner to read the package.
- Every class must be written out inside `cx(...)`, or it won't reach the stylesheet. A test compares every recipe's output with the built file.
